annote: Exposé2, six pages. Talk27 January1956; collected volume publication1957 according to bibliographic history. HA3 connected exhaustive filtration read directly; later exposés6–8 are not present here.

title: Exemples d’hyperalgèbres

annote: Exposé3 primary PDF opened locally; Proposition8 gives injectivity of the enveloping map. It does not supply the unrestricted surjectivity of the abbreviated archive checklist.

author: Jean-Louis Loday
annote: Theorem4.1.3, printedp56, read directly: characteristic-zero connected cocommutative Hopf algebra versus enveloping algebra. First arXiv circulation28 November2006; Astérisque publication2008.

title: A computational approach to the discriminant of homogeneous polynomials

annote: First arXiv17 October2012. Proposition4.7 coefficient degree and Proposition4.13 coordinate character read; final journal metadata not established here.

title: Local domains with bad sets of formal prime divisors

annote: Author’s bibliography opened and metadata verified. Full original proof not read; exact nonopen-regular-locus application checked through later sources and recorded with that limitation.

title: A few examples of local rings, I
author: Jun-ichi Nishimura
annote: Metadata found through bibliography records; direct Project Euclid PDF attempts returned an access page. This is partI (2012), not partII (2016). The full proof was not read.

title: When is the flat locus of a morphism open?
author: Takumi Murayama and other MathOverflow contributors
annote: Question and answer opened. Murayama answer13 October2025 supplies the Frobenius/bad-regular-locus route. Used as a discovery and application source; primary Kunz and Stacks results distinguish the finite-presentation case.

title: Characterizations of regular local rings of characteristic p
author: Ernst Kunz
annote: Primary bibliography opening returned403. The exact Frobenius criterion was read in Stacks tag0EC0; not cited as a1963 Jouanolou reference.

title: Direct products of modules

annote: Bibliography search retrieved metadata. The product-of-flat-modules equivalence with coherence was directly read in Stacks tag05CU; the original article proof was not reread.
journal: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society

title: On quasi algebraic closure

annote: Cited explicitly in the supplied offprint and located bibliographically. The exact gap alleged by the margin has not been identified in an opened copy of Lang’s proof.

title: Local Rings

title: Structure of local homomorphisms

annote: Author-university publication record opened; Journal of Algebra164,124–145. Modern Cohen-factorization background; exact complete factorization was read in Stacks09Q9 and07NN.

title: Natural Operations in Differential Geometry

annote: Author-hosted corrected online version2005 opened. §§14.6,14.8 pp.140–141: finite-order natural smooth bundles and jet-group actions. Different category from the archive’s arbitrary-base scheme question.

title: Noetherian approximation of algebraic spaces and stacks
author: David Rydh
annote: arXiv metadata and theorem scope opened; first circulation1 April2009, journal15 January2015. Finite-presentation/approximation-type hypotheses retained.

title: Submersions and effective descent of étale morphisms
author: David Rydh
annote: First arXiv12 October2007; final publication date not established here. Exact scope separates universally subtrusive hypotheses from arbitrary universal submersions.

title: The Picard scheme

annote: Primary author exposition opened, including representability hypotheses and Remark5.24 nonprojective abelian examples. Lectures July2003; first arXiv1 April2005.

title: Fondements de la géométrie algébrique: commentaires
author: Alexander Grothendieck
annote: Collected FGA comment text opened; dated May1962 and explaining the eight1957–1962 Bourbaki exposés. Exposés182,195,236 are also backward references in Oort. No unquoted complete proof from those exposés is assumed.

annote: Publisher metadata opened; copyright1990, hardcover publication9 January1991. TheoremI.1.9 located through Brion and Robert; original theorem proof not read.

title: Which algebraic groups are Picard varieties?
author: Michel Brion
annote: §3.1 p.466 explicitly uses dual abelian schemes without projectivity, citing Faltings–ChaiI.1.9; locally noetherian base. Online28 July2014, printMarch2015.

title: Theory of abelian varieties and their moduli spaces
author: Damien Robert
annote: Author notes, March2021 with draft version7 March2023. Theorems2.3.2 and2.3.7 pp.12–15 read. The source is unfinished lecture notes; the original Raynaud/Faltings–Chai theorem was not independently re-proved.

title: The cohomology rings of moduli stacks of principal bundles over curves
author: Jochen Heinloth and Alexander Schmitt
annote: Primary PDF opened in search027/032: §2.1 Proposition2.1.1 p.426, smooth projective curve over locally noetherian base and reductive G.

title: Sur la classification des fibrés holomorphes sur la sphère de Riemann
author: Alexander Grothendieck
annote: Primary collected-work PDF opened. Sphere/vector-bundle splitting is a special case; it does not resolve the arbitrary relative P1 question.

title: Finite group schemes, local moduli for abelian varieties, and lifting problems
author: Frans Oort
annote: Theorem2.2.1 p.273 and proofpp.277–280 read; result attributed to Grothendieck, formal smoothness of unpolarized deformations of relative dimensiong². Oslo lectures5–25 August1970; publication1971.

title: Serre–Tate local moduli
author: Nicholas M. Katz
annote: Theorem2.1 read: ordinary abelian varieties and formal torus. Orsay seminar1976–1978; publication1981. Does not replace the unrestricted unpolarized deformation theorem.

title: Interchanging direct products with tensor
annote: Propositions10.89.2–3 and their proofs read19November2026: finite generation iff all tensor/product maps are surjective; finite presentation iff they are bijective. This corrects one present-run commentary sentence, not the manuscript.

title: Flat modules and flat ring maps
annote: Definition10.39.1 and Lemmas10.39.4,10.39.7 read19November2026: exactness, flat composition and flat base change. Used only for the specified flatness components of C079/C081.

author: The Stacks Project Authors
title: Finite projective modules: Lemma10.78.2
annote: Statement and local-free/direct-summand proof steps read19November2026. Used for the finite-projective rank criterion; not an arbitrary-module projectivity theorem.

author: The Stacks Project Authors
title: Nakayama’s lemma: Lemma10.20.1
annote: Parts(2),(6),(9)–(11) and their proof mechanisms read19November2026. Finite and nilpotent variants kept distinct. Used for the stated supporting steps, not as a complete source for the manuscript’s topological or graded theorems.

author: Nicholas Katz
title: Étude cohomologique des pinceaux de Lefschetz, SGA7II, ExposéXVIII
booktitle: Groupes de monodromie en géométrie algébrique, II
annote: Original PDF visually inspected19November2026: author/notes credit printedp254, definition and conjectureXVIII5.2.2–5.2.2.1 pp281–282 (physical260,287–288). Katz is printed author, based on succinct Grothendieck notes. The exact name Lefschetz vache matches Deligne’s1966 phrase; the publication does not prove that the letter intended every later stated hypothesis. Publication1973; exact first circulation not established.

author: Pierre Deligne
title: La conjecture de Weil : II
annote: Metadata opened and original PDF visually inspected19November2026. Theorem4.1.1 and proof4.1.2–4.1.4, printedpp217–218 (physical82–83), give smooth projective pure-dimensional hard Lefschetz for an ample class over an algebraically closed field and Q_l coefficients, l different from the characteristic; Tate twists are suppressed after a chosen trivialization. Received1June1979; volume publication1980; Numdam catalogue date28December1980. These are not established first-circulation dates. Global weight/semisimplicity inputs were not reproved in this run.
